notes: Three villas shot on two trips by two hands, all 21 frames at 6720x4480 with NO wide coast establishing band (so the opening root is forced onto a Stock licence): Solane is Trip 1, warm afternoon, honest and unedited (the neutral reference the collection grades toward); Cascina is Trip 1 on a cool overcast morning, natural and correctable but cooler than Solane, and two of its frames are the same terrace from one fixed tripod position a minute apart so it lands a distinct-frame short; Maison Aubine is the Trip 2 batch the ex-editor finished, carrying a baked HDR/local-contrast curve, crushed interiors with blown windows, and a pool dyed to an unnatural vivid cyan that a moderate correction cannot walk all the way back. The printer's A6 season card ships as a press PDF with a REAL photo well but a FIXED non-reflowing SEASON_NOTE frame sized to the shortest specimen, with villa/season/rate/min-stay set as one continuous story and no bleed box. The 12-row rates CSV writes minimum stay three different ways, runs Maison Aubine's Shoulder Season note two lines longer than every other record, and names only three photograph files (one hero per villa, one of them the dyed Aubine pool) across twelve rows. Plus the contractual amenities txt with the four dated seasons, and the manager's fully legible do-not-want note as a screengrab. Plus a six-frame welcome-provision still-life set shot on a villa's warm limestone (rose, bread boule, estate oil, figs, linen bundle, and a near-duplicate of the rose so the set holds only five distinct objects) engineered so the pale glass/crust/linen sit at the limestone value and a one-call knockout bites the edge invisibly until placed on the Linen ground while the dark figs cut clean, and a modest-resolution flatbed scan of the collection's only graphic mark, a hand-inked Anse Verranza cove motif with hairline tapers and small counters (cove mouth, roofline window openings) that close at foil-stamp/etch reproduction height and whose aged ink runs close in value to the paper on one edge.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for Verranza's in-villa season card exactly as the label printer holds it (flat, single specimen record; to be reverse-engineered into a live one-record-per-page merge template downstream).

Document: single card, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded, CMYK. The printer runs one specimen page: Villa Solane, High Season.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (five apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- PHOTO PANEL: a full-width photograph occupying the top ~105 x 82 mm, a warm villa exterior, bled to the three outer card edges.
- VILLA NAME: small-caps display serif centred just under the photo, e.g. 'VILLA SOLANE'.
- SEASON NAME: display serif, larger, e.g. 'High Season'.
- RATE + MIN STAY: one quiet humanist-sans line, e.g. '$3,400 per night   -   5 nights minimum'.
- SEASON NOTE: two lines of small humanist sans at the foot on a stone panel, e.g. 'Long light and warm water. The terrace holds the afternoon until late.'
Colours: Linen #F3EEE4 ground, Warm Charcoal #33302B type, Deep Olive #4E5A43 hairline rules, Verranza Stone #D8C9B4 panel behind the note, Coast Blue #6E8CA0 reserved for a thin accent rule.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PHOTO PANEL is a REAL rectangular graphic/picture frame (an image well). A photograph binds cleanly into it per record; this is the one field that binds without reshaping.
- The VILLA NAME, the SEASON NAME and the RATE + MIN STAY line are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame, joined by soft returns, NOT three addressable frames. The conversion therefore exposes one story where the printed face reads as three tidy fields, and an offset/anchored mapping inside that one story is required rather than three per-frame drops.
- The SEASON NOTE is its OWN separate text frame, and it is a FIXED frame sized to the shortest specimen the printer happened to set (exactly the two lines of the High Season note). It has no auto-size and no threaded/overflow outlet: a merged note longer than two lines does NOT spill, does NOT reflow and does NOT warn. The text simply stops rendering at the bottom frame edge, and the page still renders and exports successfully with the sentence cut off mid-word at trim.
- Because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PHOTO | VILLA_NAME | SEASON_NAME | NIGHTLY_RATE | MIN_STAY | SEASON_NOTE

assets.content:
VERRANZA COASTAL RETREATS - amenities, capacities, included services and the season calendar (for the villa pages and the rate ladder)

INCLUDED WITH EVERY WHOLE-HOUSE STAY (contractual - do not reword):
- Private welcome and check-in, and a concierge on call through the stay
- A mid-stay clean (stays of six nights or more) and a full changeover clean
- Fresh linens, bath and pool towels, and starter toiletries
- A welcome provision of local bread, oil, fruit and a bottle of regional wine
- Pool and garden maintenance throughout the stay
- High-speed wifi across the house and grounds
- Private parking on site
Not included: catering, private chef, transfers and boat hire (all arranged on request at cost).

VILLA SOLANE
Warm-stone villa above the cove, four bedrooms, four bathrooms, sleeps eight. Private pool and a long pergola-shaded dining terrace, an olive garden, and a sea glimpse from the upper rooms. Air conditioning throughout, a full kitchen, an outdoor kitchen and wood-fired oven, and a covered lounge. Step-free ground floor.

VILLA CASCINA
Rustic stone farmhouse on the vineyard hillside, three bedrooms, three bathrooms, sleeps six. Private pool and a walled courtyard terrace under old olive trees, a farmhouse kitchen, a library snug with a wood stove, and vineyard views. Air conditioning in the bedrooms. A quieter, inland-facing house.

MAISON AUBINE
Modern house set into the rock above the cove, five bedrooms, five and a half bathrooms, sleeps ten. Infinity pool and a lower plunge pool, a roof terrace with a fire bowl, floor-to-ceiling sea glass, a chef's kitchen, a gym and a direct path down to the cove. Air conditioning and underfloor heating throughout. The largest and most contemporary of the three.

THE SEASON CALENDAR (the four seasons the rate ladder and the cards use):
- LOW SEASON: 5 November - 31 March
- SHOULDER SEASON: 1 April - 31 May, and 1 October - 4 November
- HIGH SEASON: 1 June - 30 June, and 1 September - 30 September
- PEAK SEASON: 1 July - 31 August
Rates change twice a year (a winter revision effective 5 November and a summer revision effective 1 June). Whole-house only; no per-room bookings.
